question: On 9 February 2024, two Guardia Civil officers died and two others were injured after their boat was rammed by drug traffickers in a deadly attack in the port of Barbate (Cádiz). The killed Guardia Civil officers were travelling in a small inflatable vessel, which was rammed by the drug traffickers’ 14metre speedboat.

Organised crime groups pose an increasingly direct threat to authorities and there is evidence that these criminal networks are also becoming more violent. According to the Unified Association of Civil Guards (AUGC), more than 40 % of civil guards’ absences result from physical assault.
Attacks are becoming more frequent in areas affected by drug trafficking, such as the provinces of Cádiz and Málaga, or in border regions such as Ceuta and Melilla. 1.

What studies and initiatives does the European Agency for Safety and Health at Work (EUOSHA) – whose aim is to increase knowledge, raise awareness and exchange information and good practices – have on the occupational safety of law enforcement officers?
Has EU-OSHA detected an increase in attacks on law enforcement officers also in other Member States?
Has EU-OSHA considered issuing recommendations for countries with the most alarming figures?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.3.2024) 1. The European Agency for Safety and Health at Work (EU-OSHA) has not undertaken studies or analysis on the specific issue of violence against law enforcement officers. However, the EU OSH Framework Directive1 applies to all sectors of activities and to all professions, including law enforcement officers.

It addresses all risks, including those of third-party violence. In accordance with the Framework Directive the employer has to assess all risks to which workers are or can be exposed and to establish the resulting preventive and protective measures.

Therefore, it is the responsibility of the employer (Articles 5(1) and 6(1) of the Framework Directive) to decide which preventive and protective measures should be taken in given circumstances based on a risk assessment.

In 2023, EU-OSHA has launched the Online interactive Risk Assessment (OiRA) third-party violence tool to help enterprises identify and manage the safety and health risks associated with third-party violence, and implement appropriate preventive measures to safeguard their workers. 2.

Given the absence of a specific study and research regarding the particular issue of attacks on law enforcement officers in Spain or other Member States, EU-OSHA holds no specific data or information regarding an increase in attacks on this category of workers. 3.
EU-OSHA does not issue recommendations to Member States, however it provides tools and guidelines, including good practices and publications mentioning third-party violence in general2.
1 Directive 89/391/EEC on the introduction of measures to encourage improvements in the safety and health of

workers at work, OJ L 183, 29.6.1989, p. 1. 2 Healthy Workplaces Good Practice Awards 2014–2015, https://osha.europa.eu/en/publications/healthyworkplaces-good-practice-awards-2014-2015; Third party violence in the workplace, https://osha.europa.eu/en/tools-and-publications/infographics/third-party-violence-workplace; OSHwiki Workplace violence, https://oshwiki.osha.europa.eu/en/themes/workplace-violence; Factsheet 24 - Violence at work, https://osha.europa.eu/en/publications/factsheet-24-violence-work
